analysis.title: Meritage Homes Corp. (MTH): 3Q26 First Take
key_insights: MTH reported 3Q26 EPS of $1.11 ex-charges, below GS estimate of $1.13 and FactSet consensus of $1.17.
Homebuilding (HB) revenue fell 17% YoY (units -14%, ASP -4%) vs GS forecast of -10% (units -9%, ASP -1%), a ($0.08) hit to EPS versus the estimate.
Adjusted HB EBIT (including amortized interest) was 7.0%, 36bps above GS model, adding $0.05. Taxes added $0.07 and interest and other expenses subtracted $0.06.

GS says results reflect greater demand pressure as mortgage rates hit 7.5%. Adjusted gross margin of 17.9% was largely in line with the ~18% guide, which GS credits to management balancing pace against profitability.
Unit orders fell 15% YoY vs GS estimate of -5% (and +4% a year ago). The West was down 19% and Central down 12%.
Community count grew 7% while sales pace contracted 21% YoY to 3.0/month, the low end of management's 3-4/month target. Ending backlog fell 5%, giving 1.3 months of visibility on GS estimates.

Net debt/capital rose to 19% from 17% both sequentially and YoY. Management moderated land spend further, spending $329mn on land acquisition and development (-38% YoY) and adding nearly 2,000 lots for a total of ~71,800.
The company repurchased 0.8mn shares for $55mn, with $229mn left on the authorization.
GS rates MTH Buy with a $82 12-month price target, based on 1.0x NTM tangible book value. The stock closed at $62.02, implying 32.2% upside.

GS lists questions for the call: spec inventories and 4Q starts, price elasticity and incentive effectiveness, competitive landscape into year-end, cycle times and material and labor costs, progress on the move-up shift, and land market conditions and community count growth.

market_movers.rationale: Buy and $82 target (1.0x NTM tangible book) maintained after a 3Q26 EPS and orders miss. GS cites margin discipline and conservative capital allocation.

sector_views.rationale: The report shows demand pressure from 7.5% mortgage rates, elevated incentives and limited visibility, though it takes no explicit sector stance.

earnings_insights: MTH 3Q26 reported EPS $1.11 ex-charges vs GS estimate $1.13 and FactSet consensus $1.17 (reported 10/28/2026, a miss on both).
MTH 3Q26 HB revenue -17% YoY (units -14%, ASP -4%) vs GS estimate of -10% (units -9%, ASP -1%).
MTH 3Q26 adjusted gross margin 17.9% vs ~18% company guide. Adjusted HB EBIT incl. amortized interest was 7.0%, 36bps above GS model.
MTH 3Q26 net unit orders -15% YoY vs GS estimate of -5%. Sales pace 3.0/month, down 21% YoY. Ending backlog -5% YoY.
GS estimates: 4Q26E EPS $1.45, 1Q27E EPS $0.90, FY26E EPS $4.75, FY27E EPS $5.20, FY28E EPS $6.85 (GS forecasts, not reported).

macro_indicators.interpretation: GS cites mortgage rates reaching 7.5% as a driver of weaker demand and lower orders at MTH.

risk_factors: Incentives stay higher for longer, pressuring margins.
Greater-than-expected inflation in land, labor, or materials.
Delays or limitations related to permitting and construction limiting community growth.
Limited visibility and further deterioration in demand conditions.
